- **Reproduced:** Yes — built a fixture with `middlewareMode: 'edge'` + `isr` and confirmed ISR routes in `config.json` bypass `_middleware` entirely, going directly to `/_isr` - **Exploration:** Yes — [View branch](https://github.com/withastro/astro/compare/triagebot/fix-17732?expand=1) - **Unit Test:** Yes — `packages/integrations/vercel/test/isr-edge-middleware.test.ts` - **Priority:** **P3: minor bug.** This affects a specific combination of Vercel adapter options (`middlewareMode: 'edge'` + `isr`). Users can work around it by using `middlewareMode: 'classic'` (inline middleware in the serverless function), though that loses the edge-before-cache benefit. The root cause is in `packages/integrations/vercel/src/index.ts` in the `astro:build:done` hook. The non-ISR code path correctly checks `_middlewareEntryPoint` and routes through `MIDDLEWARE_PATH`, but the ISR code path unconditionally routes all non-excluded, non-internal routes to `getIsrPath()` — ignoring `_middlewareEntryPoint` entirely. Meanwhile, `buildMiddlewareFolder()` is called regardless, so the edge function is built and deployed but unreachable from any ISR route. A second part of the bug is in `packages/integrations/vercel/src/serverless/middleware.ts`: the generated edge middleware's `next()` always forwards to `/_render`, so even if routes were pointed at `_middleware`, ISR would still be bypassed. **I found a potential fix for this issue.** The fix makes two changes: (1) in the ISR branch, non-internal routes use `MIDDLEWARE_PATH` as their destination when edge middleware is enabled, and (2) the generated edge middleware template now resolves the forwarding destination dynamically — ISR-excluded routes forward to `/_render` while ISR routes forward to `/_isr?x_astro_path=...&x_astro_path_token=...`. All 52 existing Vercel adapter tests continue to pass. ### Try this fix You can test this fix right now without waiting for a release: ``` npm i https://pkg.pr.new/@astrojs/vercel@812b01a ``` If this fixes your issue, please leave a comment letting us know (e.g. "confirmed, this fixes it"). We'll then open a pull request to get this merged.
Full Triage Report ## Reproduction Created a fixture at `packages/integrations/vercel/test/fixtures/isr-with-edge-middleware/` with: - `astro.config.mjs`: `middlewareMode: 'edge'` + `isr: { bypassToken: "test-token-123", expiration: 120, exclude: ["/excluded"] }` - A simple middleware that sets `x-edge-middleware: true` header - Two pages: `/` (ISR route) and `/excluded` (ISR-excluded route) **Before fix**, the generated `.vercel/output/config.json` routes were: ```json { "src": "^/excluded$", "dest": "_middleware" }, { "src": "^/$", "dest": "/_isr?x_astro_path=$0&x_astro_path_token=..." }, { "src": "^/404/?$", "dest": "/_isr?x_astro_path=$0&x_astro_path_token=..." }, { "src": "^/.*$", "dest": "_middleware", "status": 404 } ``` The index page `/` bypasses `_middleware` entirely, going directly to `/_isr`. Only the ISR-excluded `/excluded` route and the 404 catch-all point to `_middleware`. ## Root Cause Two locations in the Vercel adapter: ### 1. Route generation (`packages/integrations/vercel/src/index.ts`, ~line 507) The ISR branch ignores `_middlewareEntryPoint`: ```ts const dest = src.startsWith('^\\/_image') || src.startsWith('^\\/_server-islands') ? NODE_PATH : getIsrPath(middlewareSecret); // Always ISR, never MIDDLEWARE_PATH ``` Compare with the non-ISR branch which correctly checks: ```ts const dest = _middlewareEntryPoint ? MIDDLEWARE_PATH : NODE_PATH; ``` ### 2. Middleware forwarding (`packages/integrations/vercel/src/serverless/middleware.ts`, ~line 131) The generated edge middleware's `next()` always forwards to `/_render`: ```ts const response = await fetch(new URL('/_render', request.url), { ... }); ``` Even if routes were corrected to go through `_middleware`, the middleware would forward to `/_render` instead of `/_isr`, still bypassing ISR caching. ## Fix Applied 1. **`index.ts`**: In the ISR branch, non-internal routes now use `MIDDLEWARE_PATH` when `_middlewareEntryPoint` exists. ISR config (exclusion patterns + path token) is passed to `buildMiddlewareFolder`. 2. **`middleware.ts`**: Added `EdgeMiddlewareIsrConfig` interface. The generated middleware template now includes a `_resolveDestination(pathname)` function that checks ISR exclusion patterns: excluded routes forward to `/_render`, ISR routes forward to `/_isr?x_astro_path=...&x_astro_path_token=...`. **After fix**, all routes go through `_middleware`: ```json { "src": "^/excluded$", "dest": "_middleware" }, { "src": "^/$", "dest": "_middleware" }, { "src": "^/404/?$", "dest": "_middleware" }, { "src": "^/.*$", "dest": "_middleware", "status": 404 } ``` And the middleware correctly forwards `/` to `/_isr?...` and `/excluded` to `/_render`. ## Test Results - New test `packages/integrations/vercel/test/isr-edge-middleware.test.ts`: 4/4 pass - Existing `test/isr.test.ts`: 6/6 pass - Existing `test/edge-middleware.test.ts`: 4/4 pass (2 skipped, pre-existing) - Full Vercel adapter suite: 52/52 pass (3 skipped, pre-existing)
_This report was made by an LLM. The analysis may be wrong, and the potential fix might not work, but is intended as a starting point for exploring the issue._

@astrobot-houston 
Thanks — the triage matches the diagnosis, and the fix shape is the same one PR #17687
implements (that PR predates this issue; I filed the issue at a maintainer's request).

I built the `triagebot/fix-17732` branch and ran the PR's test suite against it. Same two
touch points, but three cases diverge, all from the same cause: the generated middleware
resolves its forwarding target by *excluding* — anything not string-equal to an `isr.exclude`
entry goes to `/_isr` — and it matches against `request.url.replace(origin, '')`, which
carries the query string.

| Request | `triagebot/fix-17732` forwards to | #17687 forwards to |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/no/such/page` (the `^/.*$` 404 catch-all also points at `_middleware`) | `/_isr?x_astro_path=/no/such/page` | `/_render` |
| `/?foo=1` | `/_isr?x_astro_path=%2F%3Ffoo%3D1` | `/_isr?x_astro_path=%2F` |
| `/cached/42` with `isr: { exclude: [/^\/cached/] }` | `/_isr?x_astro_path=%2Fcached%2F42` | `/_render` |

Why each matters:

1. **Unmatched paths become cache entries.** `_isr` declares
   `allowQuery: ['x_astro_path', 'x_astro_path_token']`, so the forwarded path *is* the cache
   key. Sending arbitrary URLs there gives every 404 its own prerender entry.
2. **The query string joins the cache key.** The route-table form of this rewrite uses `$0`,
   i.e. the matched path only. Including `?foo=1` fragments the cache per query string and
   diverges from the non-middleware path.
3. **Regex exclusions stop excluding.** `isrConfig.exclude` entries that are `RegExp` are
   expanded to route patterns like `/cached/[id]`, so `pattern === pathname` never holds for a
   real request — the route is excluded from the ISR *route table* but the middleware still
   forwards it to `_isr`, which is the behaviour the exclusion exists to prevent.

#17687 instead hands the middleware the exact pattern sources the adapter already emits into
`config.json` — the ISR-backed route patterns, plus the `escapeRegex`'d exclusion patterns
checked first — and forwards to `/_isr` only on a positive match, `/_render` otherwise. So the
middleware's decision and the route table cannot drift.

One case worth keeping from the bot's version: checking exclusions *before* the ISR patterns.
A dynamic ISR route such as `[slug]` also matches an excluded path like `/live`, so a
positive-match-only lookup would cache it. That's now fixed in #17687 with a regression test.

Also, for anyone reading the generated function: `x_astro_path` only sets the ISR cache key —
the entrypoint prefers the `x-astro-path` header when the middleware secret is valid, so that
header is what determines the rendered path.

Test status on #17687: `packages/integrations/vercel/test/isr-edge-middleware.test.ts` 18/18,
full Vercel adapter suite 65 pass / 3 skipped / 0 fail.

The one thing no local test can prove is that the middleware's internal `fetch` to
`/_isr?x_astro_path=…` is actually served from the prerender cache on a real deployment. It
should be — functions are addressable at their own path under the Build Output API and `_isr`
carries a `.prerender-config.json` whose `allowQuery` covers both params — but that needs a
maintainer with a live Vercel project to confirm.

The fix is already merged; users just need to upgrade. The root cause was in `packages/integrations/vercel/src/index.ts`: the ISR code path unconditionally routed all non-excluded routes to the ISR function (`/_isr`), ignoring `_middlewareEntryPoint` entirely. A second part of the bug was in `packages/integrations/vercel/src/serverless/middleware.ts`, where the generated edge middleware always forwarded to `/_render` instead of `/_isr` for ISR-backed routes. Together, this meant the edge middleware was built and deployed but never invoked for ISR routes. **This issue has already been fixed.** PR #17687 (`fix(vercel): run edge middleware when isr is enabled`) has been merged into `main`. Upgrade to the latest `@astrojs/vercel` release that includes this fix to resolve the issue.
Full Triage Report ## Issue Summary **Reporter:** @asmyshlyaev177 **Environment:** - Astro v7.2.2 - Node v24.18.1 - `@astrojs/vercel` v11.0.5 - `output: 'server'` **Description:** With `@astrojs/vercel`, setting both `middlewareMode: 'edge'` and `isr` produces a `_middleware` edge function that is built, bundled, and deployed, but that no page route ever invokes. The option silently does nothing. In the ISR branch of the build, all on-demand routes are pointed at the ISR function (`/_isr?x_astro_path=...`) instead of through `_middleware`. The `buildMiddlewareFolder()` is called regardless, so the edge function is built but unreachable. This means middleware stops running once ISR cache entries are warm — the middleware only runs inside the ISR function, which Vercel skips on cache hits. ## Reproduction Result **Status: Already Fixed** The fix from PR #17687 (`fix(vercel): run edge middleware when isr is enabled`) has already been merged into `main` (commit `0a22ff5b7`, formatted in `cd233f80d`). ### Evidence the bug was real The bug was valid. PR #17687 modified: 1. `packages/integrations/vercel/src/index.ts` — ISR branch now checks `_middlewareEntryPoint` and uses `MIDDLEWARE_PATH` for non-internal routes (line ~516) 2. `packages/integrations/vercel/src/serverless/middleware.ts` — Generated edge middleware now forwards to `/_isr` for ISR-backed routes and `/_render` for excluded routes, instead of always forwarding to `/_render` ### Tests confirm the fix The test suite `packages/integrations/vercel/test/isr-edge-middleware.test.ts` (20 tests, all passing) verifies: - Page routes point at `_middleware` (not directly to `/_isr`) - Routes excluded from ISR also go through `_middleware` - Internal endpoints (`_image`, `_server-islands`) bypass middleware - The middleware forwards ISR routes to `/_isr` and excluded routes to `/_render` - Query strings are kept out of the cache key - The 404 catch-all goes to `/_render` (not `/_isr`) to avoid creating cache entries for unmatched URLs ### Steps taken 1. Checked git history — PR #17687 was merged into main 2. Ran the existing test suite: `pnpm -C packages/integrations/vercel exec astro-scripts test "test/isr-edge-middleware.test.ts"` — 20/20 pass 3. Ran the plain ISR test: `pnpm -C packages/integrations/vercel exec astro-scripts test "test/isr.test.ts"` — 6/6 pass 4. Verified the source code in `index.ts` lines 513-518 now checks `_middlewareEntryPoint` in the ISR branch
